quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: Not having the same advantages, especially money and status, as most people in society.
Having a great deal of money; wealthy.
The social group consisting of people who work for wages, especially in manual or industrial jobs.
The social group between the working class and the upper class, often including professionals.
A select group considered to be the best or most powerful within a society.

quests.hint: Each word or phrase names a different position within society's economic ladder.
quests.explanation: Underprivileged and affluent sit at opposite ends of that ladder, one lacking advantage, the other having plenty. Working class and middle class describe two broad groups in between, often distinguished by the kind of work they do. Elite is different from the rest — a small, powerful group at the very top, defined by influence as much as by money.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: A situation where one party has more or better information than another.
Deserving of trust and confidence; reliable.
The small, often overlooked text in a contract that contains important details or restrictions.
A warning that the buyer alone is responsible for checking the quality of a purchase.
A warning sign that something may be wrong.

quests.hint: Each word or phrase relates to trust, or the lack of it, in a deal or agreement.
quests.explanation: Information asymmetry describes an unfair starting point, one side knowing more than the other, and fine print is where that imbalance often hides. Buyer beware is the blunt warning that follows, placing the responsibility on you, and a red flag is the actual sign that something's wrong. Trustworthy is different from the rest — it's the reassuring quality all of this caution is ultimately looking for.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: A work that honors or shows respect for another creator's style or work.
A humorous imitation of a work, style, or genre, exaggerated for comic effect.
A new version of an existing work presented from a different creative angle.
Combining elements from different genres in a single creative work.
A recognizable and unique way a writer expresses their ideas.

quests.hint: Each word or phrase relates to how a creative work borrows from, changes, or defines itself against others.
quests.explanation: Homage and parody both echo an existing work, though homage does so respectfully while parody exaggerates it for laughs. Reinterpretation takes that same borrowed material and reshapes it from a new angle, and genre-bending mixes categories together instead. Distinctive style is different from the rest — it's about originality, a voice that doesn't borrow from anything else at all.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: The exhaustion experienced by people repeatedly subjected to subtle discrimination.
Discrimination against women embedded in laws, institutions, and cultural norms.
Policies favoring historically underrepresented groups in employment or education.
Discrimination against people with disabilities.
Active opposition to racism through deliberate policy, education, and personal action.

quests.hint: These phrases all tie back to a form of discrimination, or an active effort to correct it.
quests.explanation: Structural sexism and ableism both describe discrimination built into everyday systems, one based on gender, the other on disability. Microaggression fatigue is the toll that kind of repeated discrimination takes on a person. Affirmative action and anti-racism are different from the rest — deliberate responses meant to correct injustice, not forms of injustice themselves.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: The natural drive to stay alive and avoid danger.
Coloring or a pattern that allows an animal to blend into its surroundings.
A state of reduced activity that helps an organism survive unfavorable conditions.
A state of inactivity some animals enter to survive winter, with lowered body temperature.
The complete disappearance of a species from the Earth.

quests.hint: Each word or phrase relates to how living things survive, or fail to survive, in nature.
quests.explanation: Survival instinct drives every strategy that follows, including camouflage, which helps an animal avoid being seen. Dormancy and hibernation both slow the body down to conserve energy, though hibernation is a specific seasonal form of that same idea. Extinction is different from the rest — it's the outcome when none of these survival strategies are enough.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: The physical features of an area of land.
A set of numbers used to indicate the exact position of a point on a map.
The height of a place above sea level.
The science and practice of drawing maps.
One of the four main directions — north, south, east, or west — used for navigation.

quests.hint: Each word or phrase relates to understanding and describing a place on a map.
quests.explanation: Cartography is the whole skill of mapmaking, and coordinates and compass direction are two of its essential tools, pinpointing and orienting a location. Elevation adds a third dimension to that picture, height above sea level, and terrain is different from the rest — the actual physical landscape being mapped, not a tool used to describe it.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: A duty or obligation held collectively by a group of people.
A shared asset, such as a park or library, available for public use.
Able to provide for oneself without outside help.
The process of reaching general agreement within a group.
The ability of a community or region to govern itself independently.

quests.hint: Each of these phrases points to how a community manages itself and what it shares.
quests.explanation: Shared responsibility often centers on a community resource, something the whole group relies on together. Consensus building is how decisions about that resource typically get made fairly, and local autonomy is what allows a community to make those decisions in the first place, without outside interference. Self-sufficient is different from the rest — it describes independence from needing others at all, not cooperation with them.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: A person who continues or returns to education after typical school age.
An approach where the learner takes initiative in identifying their own learning needs.
Learning by physically doing a task rather than just studying it theoretically.
Using a skill or piece of knowledge in an actual, practical situation.
A person's preferred way of taking in and processing new information.

quests.hint: Each phrase relates to how adults, specifically, learn best.
quests.explanation: An adult learner often benefits most from self-directed learning, taking charge of their own goals and pace. Hands-on practice and real-world application both reinforce that learning through doing, not just studying. Learning style is different from the rest — it's about individual preference in how information is absorbed, not a method or type of learner.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: The way a person's attitudes or behavior are affected by others.
Behavior that matches the accepted standards or expectations of a group.
The existing state of affairs, especially regarding social or political issues.
Ideas, attitudes, or activities regarded as normal or conventional by most of society.
Public disagreement with an official or widely held opinion.

quests.hint: Each word or phrase relates to how ideas spread, settle, or get challenged in society.
quests.explanation: Social influence shapes conformity, encouraging people to match what's mainstream and widely accepted. Together, these forces help maintain the status quo, keeping things as they are. Dissent is different from the rest — it's the pushback against all of this, disagreement with what's already settled and accepted.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: Using data analytics to forecast and prevent crime before it occurs.
Using automated tools to assist in criminal sentencing decisions.
The rate at which previously convicted criminals reoffend.
Removing criminal penalties for an activity while not fully legalizing it.
Non-custodial supervision of offenders in the community.

quests.hint: Each phrase ties back to how modern justice systems try to prevent or respond to crime.
quests.explanation: Predictive policing and algorithmic sentencing both bring data into the justice system, one before a crime happens, the other after. Recidivism rate measures whether any of this actually works, tracking how often people reoffend. Decriminalization and community corrections are different from the rest — both represent softer approaches, moving away from strict punishment rather than predicting or judging crime.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: The forcing of people to leave their homes or communities, often due to economic pressure.
Housing priced within reach of people with low to moderate incomes.
The shared sense of belonging and characteristics that define a neighborhood or group.
The process of rebuilding or renovating an area, often changing its character.
A strong feeling of respect and satisfaction people have for the area where they live.

quests.hint: Every one of these phrases connects to how a neighborhood changes, and what can be gained or lost.
quests.explanation: Redevelopment can reshape a neighborhood's character, and displacement is a serious risk if that change pushes out longtime residents. Affordable housing is one way to guard against that risk, and community identity and neighborhood pride are what's ultimately at stake, the sense of belonging a place provides. Neighborhood pride is different from the rest — a feeling, not a policy or process.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: Medical treatment tailored to the individual's genetics, lifestyle, and environment.
Using the body's immune system to fight disease, especially cancer.
Identifying a disease at its earliest, most treatable stage.
Medical therapy designed to act specifically on the cause of a disease.
The measurable result of a medical treatment on a patient's health.

quests.hint: Notice how each phrase connects to modern advances in diagnosing and treating serious illness.
quests.explanation: Precision medicine and targeted treatment both tailor care to the individual, rather than a one-size-fits-all approach. Immunotherapy is one specific method within that shift, and early detection improves the odds for any treatment to succeed. Clinical outcome is different from the rest — it's the final result all of this progress is measured against.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: The way something is understood or interpreted.
Something that appears to be real but is not; a false impression.
The quality of being genuine or real.
A particular interpretation of information presented to influence public opinion.
Invented or made up, rather than genuine or true.

quests.hint: Each word relates to the gap between what seems real and what actually is.
quests.explanation: Perception shapes how we understand reality, but illusion shows how easily that perception can be tricked. Spin and fabricated both describe ways truth gets deliberately distorted, one through framing, the other through outright invention. Authenticity is different from the rest — it's the genuine quality all of this distortion moves away from.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: A threshold environment between one state and another, often feeling uncanny.
The visual and physical characteristics of a city environment.
The state of being alone, often peacefully or by choice.
The particular mood or feeling created by a place or situation.
A place or thing that is little-known but especially valuable or delightful.

quests.hint: Each word or phrase relates to the feeling a particular place can create.
quests.explanation: Urban landscape sets the physical scene, and atmosphere is the mood that scene creates. A liminal space is a specific, unsettling kind of atmosphere, caught between one state and another, while a hidden gem creates the opposite feeling, quiet delight in discovery. Solitude is different from the rest — it describes a personal state of being alone, not a quality of the place itself.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: The mental processes enabling planning, working memory, and impulse control.
The ability to control one's own emotions and behavior in the face of temptation.
The length of time a person can concentrate on a task without becoming distracted.
The mental system that holds and manipulates information for a short period during a task.
The mental ability to shift thinking between concepts or adapt to new information.

quests.hint: These phrases all tie back to a specific mental skill the brain uses to manage everyday tasks.
quests.explanation: Executive function is the broad set of skills behind all focused, organized thought, including working memory and attention span, both needed to hold a task in mind. Self-control keeps behavior in check while doing so, and cognitive flexibility is different from the rest — it's about adapting between ideas, not sustaining focus or restraint.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: Preventing war through the threat of nuclear retaliation.
A doctrine where both sides' nuclear capability deters first strike.
Competitive accumulation of weapons between rival states.
A period of reduced tension between rival powers.
When one state's security measures make other states feel less secure.

quests.hint: Each of these phrases points to the tense balance nations strike to avoid war.
quests.explanation: Nuclear deterrence relies on mutually assured destruction, both sides too afraid of retaliation to strike first. That same fear can spark an arms race instead, each side building up in response to the other, exactly what the security dilemma describes. Détente is different from the rest — a period when that tension actually eases, rather than builds.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: The practice of protecting computer systems and data from digital attacks.
The crime of using someone else's personal information without permission, usually for financial gain.
A password designed to be difficult for others to guess or crack.
Manipulating people into revealing confidential information through deception.
A cyberattack targeting an unknown or unpatched software vulnerability.

quests.hint: Each phrase relates to protecting yourself, or being targeted, online.
quests.explanation: Cybersecurity covers the whole effort of staying safe online, and a secure password is one basic tool within it. Social engineering and a zero-day exploit are two different kinds of attack that can get past those defenses, one tricking a person, the other exploiting a flaw in the software itself. Identity theft is different from the rest — it's the harmful outcome, not a defense or an attack method.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: Understanding gained through direct experience rather than theory.
A test of something before it is used or done for real.
Applying a skill learned in one situation to a different, new situation.
The actual circumstances in which something happens, as opposed to theory.
The physical and social setting in which learning takes place.

quests.hint: Each phrase ties back to how learning connects, or fails to connect, to the real world.
quests.explanation: Practical knowledge grows out of real-life context, understanding built through direct experience rather than theory alone. A trial run tests that knowledge safely before it's applied for real, and skill transfer is the ultimate goal, using it successfully in a new situation. Learning environment is different from the rest — the setting where all of this learning happens, not the knowledge or skill itself.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: Thinking about what might have happened if past events had been different.
The process of drawing conclusions about cause-and-effect relationships from data.
A study where participants are randomly assigned to treatment or control groups.
An error in study design that makes a sample unrepresentative of the population.
A group in an experiment that does not receive the treatment being tested, used for comparison.

quests.hint: Every one of these phrases connects to how researchers try to prove that one thing actually causes another.
quests.explanation: Causal inference is the goal, and a randomized controlled trial is the gold-standard method used to reach it, comparing outcomes against a control group. Selection bias is a serious risk that can undermine any of this if the sample isn't fair. Counterfactual reasoning is different from the rest — a thought exercise imagining an alternative past, not a formal research method.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: The sharing of resources or benefits in a way that is just and equitable.
The best possible result achievable given the circumstances.
A method of comparing the costs and benefits of a decision to determine its value.
An influence from outside a system that affects its outcome.
A system that maintains balance and function despite outside pressures.

quests.hint: Notice how each phrase connects to judging whether a decision, or a whole system, is working well.
quests.explanation: A cost-benefit analysis is one practical way of judging a decision, aiming for the most optimal outcome possible. Fair distribution adds another standard beyond pure efficiency, making sure that outcome is also just. External factor and stable system are different from the rest — both describe the wider conditions surrounding a decision, not the decision or its fairness.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: The practice of actively restoring degraded ecosystems to their natural state.
Using living organisms to neutralize pollutants in a contaminated environment.
Controlling non-native species that threaten native ecosystems.
A strip of habitat connecting isolated patches to allow species movement.
The natural process of ecosystem development over time after disturbance.

quests.hint: These phrases all tie back to how a damaged natural environment can heal or be helped to heal.
quests.explanation: Restorative ecology guides the whole effort of repair, and bioremediation is one specific technique within it, using living organisms to clean up pollution. Invasive species management and ecological corridor both protect that recovery, removing threats and reconnecting habitats. Succession is different from the rest — it's the natural process of recovery happening on its own, without deliberate human help.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: The natural variation in human brain function, including conditions like autism.
A disability arising from mental health conditions affecting social participation.
Words or phrases that reinforce negative attitudes toward disability.
Designing products and environments usable by all people, to the greatest extent possible.
The legal and social movement advocating for equal treatment and access for disabled people.

quests.hint: Each of these phrases points to understanding, respecting, and including people with disabilities.
quests.explanation: Neurodiversity and psychosocial disability both describe real variation in human experience, one in brain function, the other tied to mental health. Ableist language can quietly undermine both, and disability rights is the movement pushing back against exactly that kind of harm. Universal design is different from the rest — a practical solution, building environments that work for everyone from the start.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: Linked together in a way that each part affects the others.
Able to be touched or perceived; real and definite, not abstract.
Not able to be touched or grasped; not having a physical presence.
A person's overall perspective on life and how it should be understood.
Involving deep, quiet thought and reflection.

quests.hint: Each word relates to how we think about, or experience, the nature of reality.
quests.explanation: Tangible and intangible are opposites, one able to be touched, the other existing only as an idea or feeling. Interconnected describes how both kinds of things, physical or not, often shape each other. Worldview and contemplative are different from the rest — worldview is the broad lens shaping all of this thinking, and contemplative describes the quiet, reflective mode of thinking itself.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: Payment for work that is delayed to a future period, such as a pension.
A one-time payment offered to a new employee as an incentive to accept a job.
The time an employee must work before becoming entitled to benefits.
Payment in the form of company shares rather than cash.
A contractual clause allowing an employer to reclaim previously paid compensation.

quests.hint: Each phrase relates to how a modern job might pay you beyond just a regular salary.
quests.explanation: A signing bonus rewards you immediately, while deferred compensation and equity compensation both pay out later, one as future cash, the other as company shares. A vesting period often controls exactly when that later payment becomes truly yours. Clawback provision is different from the rest — it works in reverse, letting an employer take payment back under certain conditions.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: Reasoning from general principles to reach a specific, logical conclusion.
Reasoning from specific examples to form a general conclusion.
A guess based on knowledge and experience, more likely to be correct than a random one.
A general, practical guideline based on experience rather than exact calculation.
Logical thinking that is valid and well-supported by evidence.

quests.hint: Each word or phrase relates to how conclusions get reached, formally or informally.
quests.explanation: Deduction and induction are two formal, opposite paths to a conclusion, one from general rule to specific case, the other from specific cases to a general rule. Educated guess and rule of thumb are more informal versions of the same instinct, useful without being fully rigorous. Sound reasoning is different from the rest — it's the standard all of these methods are ultimately judged against.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: The molecule that carries genetic information in living things.
The passing of characteristics from parents to offspring through genes.
A change in the genetic material of an organism, which can be passed on.
Any individual living thing, such as a plant, animal, or bacterium.
Too small to be seen without the aid of a microscope.

quests.hint: Each word relates to the basic building blocks of life and how they're passed on.
quests.explanation: DNA carries the information behind heredity, the passing of traits from parent to offspring. Mutation is a change within that same genetic material, sometimes passed on as well. Organism and microscopic are different from the rest — organism describes any living thing carrying DNA, and microscopic describes a scale of size, not a genetic process.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: The collective views and attitudes held by the general population on an issue.
Respectful and reasoned discussion of differing viewpoints.
The benefit or interests of all members of a community.
The right to express opinions without government restriction.
A public event or platform where people discuss shared concerns.

quests.hint: Each phrase ties back to how people discuss and shape public life together.
quests.explanation: Freedom of speech protects the right to take part, and civil discourse is how that right is ideally exercised, respectfully. A community forum is one practical setting where that discourse happens, and public opinion is often what emerges from it. Common good is different from the rest — the shared goal all of this discussion is meant to serve.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: The coexistence of multiple legal systems within a single geographic area.
When two or more legal systems claim authority over the same matter.
Rules and agreements governing relations between countries.
Law operating above national legal systems, such as European Union law.
Non-binding international norms and standards that influence behavior.

quests.hint: Every one of these phrases connects to how law operates across, or beyond, national borders.
quests.explanation: International law governs relations broadly between countries, and supranational law goes a step further, sitting above national systems entirely. Legal pluralism and jurisdictional overlap both describe complications that can arise when multiple systems apply at once. Soft law is different from the rest — it carries influence without being formally binding, unlike the others.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: The quality of being able to adjust easily to new conditions.
Collective information and know-how held within an organization, often informally.
The way an organization arranges its roles, responsibilities, and reporting lines.
Exhaustion and resistance caused by too much organizational change happening too quickly.
The ability of an organization to deliver products or services with minimal waste.

quests.hint: Notice how each phrase connects to how well an organization functions and adapts over time.
quests.explanation: Organizational structure shapes how a company operates, and operational efficiency measures how well it delivers within that structure. Adaptability determines whether that structure can adjust to change, though change fatigue shows what happens when adjustment happens too often, too fast. Institutional knowledge is different from the rest — it's the accumulated know-how held within the organization, not a measure of performance or flexibility.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: A treatment made from plants, used in traditional medicine.
Healing practices and knowledge developed within a culture over generations, often plant-based.
Relating to plants or plant life.
A land management approach integrating trees with crops or livestock.
The variety of different plant species grown for food and other uses.

quests.hint: Each word or phrase relates to the deep relationship between plants, culture, and land.
quests.explanation: Traditional medicine often relies on a herbal remedy, both drawing on the healing properties of botanical life. Agroforestry and crop diversity take that same relationship with plants in a different direction, focused on how land is farmed sustainably. Botanical is different from the rest — the broad adjective connecting all of these ideas back to plants themselves.
